threads.thread_goal: Align on sitemap, navigation, and page priorities for the redesign.

messages.text:
Kicking off sitemap work for the corporate marketing site redesign project_title: Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
I have a first pass of the page inventory and a draft sitemap based on the current site audit.

From T1, I pulled together an inventory of existing pages and templates and logged UX and visual issues. I used that to start a target sitemap in A2 (Sitemap and Page Inventory Matrix) for T2.

Top-level proposal:
- Home
- Solutions (with subpages per solution)
- Products
- Pricing
- Resources (blog, case studies, webinars)
- Company (About, Careers, Press, Contact)

Questions:
1) Are we ok merging some of the legacy marketing campaign microsites into Resources for now?
2) For navigation, I am leaning toward a single global header with primary nav and a slim utility bar for Login and Support.

Can art directors take a look at the A2 tab called Target Sitemap v1 and comment on what should be in scope for the first release vs later phases?

Thanks for sharing the first pass.
I went through A2 Target Sitemap v1 and cross-checked with the audit notes from T1.
Initial reactions:
- Top-level structure looks close to what marketing has been asking for.
- We should keep Solutions and Products clearly separated in the nav labels so visitors understand the difference.
- For the legacy campaign microsites, I would suggest we keep only the ones still driving traffic as dedicated landing pages and fold the rest into Resources.

For T2, we also need to define primary vs secondary navigation patterns. I suggest:
- Primary nav: Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources, Company
- Secondary (utility) nav: Login, Support, Language switch (if we keep it), plus a prominent CTA button for Talk to sales.

Before we lock anything, I want to make sure this aligns with how the dev team has structured things in the current WebCMS. We should not create a navigation model that is impossible to manage there.

I also reviewed A2 and the current structure from T1.
A couple of points from a brand and messaging angle:
- Can we group case studies more prominently under Resources, maybe as Customer stories, so they are easier to find from the main nav?
- Under Company, I would add a dedicated page for Trust or Security if we have enough content. That tends to be important for B2B visitors.

On the microsites question: I agree with keeping only the active ones as standalone pages. Maybe we can tag them clearly in A2 so we know which ones are in the first release vs later.

For T2, I would like to see a simple diagram of the primary and secondary nav, not just the matrix, so stakeholders can react quickly in the next review.

I left some comments directly in A2 as well.
One concern: the current sitemap draft has Pricing only at the top level. Marketing has been asking for pricing entry points from some product pages too. Maybe we should reflect that in the matrix as cross-links or secondary CTAs.

Also, for the first release scope, I suggest we prioritize:
- Home
- 2–3 highest-traffic Solutions pages
- Main Products overview
- Pricing
- Resources overview + 3–4 key case studies
- Company: About, Careers, Contact

We can leave Press and some of the long-tail Resources items for a later phase, as long as we keep redirects in mind.

Does that sound realistic for the 21-day core template timeline?

I can help by sketching the nav diagram that was mentioned.
Just to confirm: for the primary nav, we keep it to five items max, right? If we add Trust or Security under Company, that would be a subpage, not a top-level item.

For the microsites, should I mark them in A2 with a separate status like Legacy landing to keep track of redirects later, or is that handled elsewhere?

Yes, let us keep the primary nav to five items. Trust or Security would live under Company.

On A2, please add a status column if it is not there already and use something like:
- In scope v1
- In scope later
- Legacy landing (redirect)

That will help when we get to rollout planning and also when we brief the dev lead on redirects.

Once you have the nav diagram, attach a link in this thread and reference it in T2 so we can say the navigation patterns are fully defined.

I updated A2 with:
- Customer stories as a distinct content type under Resources, with a flag to surface them in the main nav.
- A Trust and Security page under Company.
- A status column as suggested, and I tagged the active campaign microsites as In scope v1 or In scope later based on the traffic notes from T1.

For Pricing, I added cross-links from the main Products overview and from the top 3 product detail pages, so we remember to design those CTAs when we get to T4 and T6.

Can you all take another quick pass and see if anything critical is missing before we present this to marketing and product?

I reviewed the latest A2 updates.
From my side, the structure now covers:
- All core marketing flows (Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources, Company)
- Key trust-building content (Customer stories, Trust and Security)
- A clear split between first release and later phases.

I do not see any major gaps for the first release. The only nuance is making sure Support is easy to find from both the header and the footer, but that is more of a layout detail for T4.

I am comfortable presenting this sitemap and nav model to stakeholders as our recommended direction.

Same here, I went through A2 and left a couple of minor comments on naming (for example, using Resources instead of Insights to stay closer to current marketing language).

For the first release scope, I suggest we explicitly list the pages in this thread so there is no confusion later.
My proposal for v1 pages:
- Home
- 3 Solutions pages (top traffic)
- Products overview + 3 key product detail pages
- Pricing
- Resources overview + 4 Customer stories
- Company: About, Careers, Contact, Trust and Security
- Support landing

Everything else in A2 would be In scope later or Legacy landing.

If we agree on this list, we can mark it in A2 and move T2 toward approval.

I like this breakdown. It is ambitious but still realistic for the 21-day core template window, since many of these pages will share templates.

To make this concrete, I just:
- Marked the v1 pages in A2 with In scope v1.
- Added a short note in the doc summary that this is our recommended MVP set.

Unless anyone sees a blocker today, I suggest we treat this sitemap structure and v1 page list as approved for design work. We can still adjust labels slightly during copy work, but the structure and scope would be fixed.

Please speak up in this thread if you disagree before end of day.

No objections from me.
The v1 list seems manageable, and having the In scope later and Legacy landing tags in A2 will help when we get to rollout planning.

I will finish the nav diagram today and align it with the approved structure so stakeholders have a visual to react to in the next review.

Works for me as well.
I will use the In scope v1 tags in A2 as the basis for the first batch of wireframes and templates under T2 and then T4.

If marketing or product push for extra pages mid-stream, we can log those as change requests and mark them In scope later unless we explicitly trade something out.

Given the feedback so far and the updates in A2, I am comfortable saying:
- The target sitemap structure is defined enough for design to proceed.
- The v1 page list that was summarized is our agreed first release scope.

I will present this in the next stakeholder touchpoint and call out that any new pages will go into the In scope later bucket unless we revisit priorities.

Summarizing this thread so we can close it out:
- Target sitemap and navigation model in A2 are approved for design.
- First release scope is the v1 page list marked In scope v1 in A2 (Home, 3 Solutions, Products overview + 3 product details, Pricing, Resources overview + 4 Customer stories, Company core pages, Support landing).
- Legacy and long-tail pages are tagged for later phases or redirects.

Next, we will move into wireframes and layout templates based on this structure.

I will update T2 as completed once the nav diagram is attached and then shift focus to T4.

threads.thread_goal: Select the visual direction and core UI components.

messages.text:
Starting the visual direction and components thread for project_title: Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.

I have uploaded two moodboard options and an initial set of core components for T3 and T5. They are documented in A3 under:
- Direction A: Clean enterprise (more white space, subtle gradients, photography-led)
- Direction B: Bold contrast (strong color blocks, more illustration, higher contrast)

Core components sketched so far:
- Buttons (primary, secondary, ghost)
- Form fields (single-line, text area, select)
- Cards (feature, resource, customer story)
- Navigation (header, footer, mobile nav)
- Banners (hero, announcement)

Please review A3 and drop comments on:
1) Which direction feels closer to our current brand while still modernizing.
2) Any missing components we should include in the first pass of the library.

I went through A3 and left inline notes.
My quick take:
- Direction A feels closer to the existing brand guidelines and will probably be easier to get approved by the brand manager.
- Direction B is visually interesting but might be a bigger leap, especially with the heavy illustration.

For components under T5, I would add:
- A compact promo strip for cross-selling between Products and Solutions.
- A testimonial module that can be reused on Solutions, Products, and the homepage.

If we choose Direction A as the base, we can still borrow some of the bolder accent colors from Direction B for CTAs and key highlights.

I also reviewed both directions in A3.
From a campaign and messaging perspective:
- Direction A will integrate more smoothly with existing assets and the current WebCMS templates.
- Direction B might require more custom illustration work and could slow us down for the first release.

I like the idea of using Direction A as the main path and selectively pulling in some of the stronger color accents from Direction B for banners and CTAs.

On components, I would also like to see a simple metrics or stats block that we can reuse on the homepage and Solutions pages.

I added a few comments in A3 from a layout and implementation angle.
Direction A should be straightforward to implement with our current WebCMS and front-end stack. Direction B has some overlapping shapes and layered elements that might be harder to reproduce consistently across templates.

For T5, I suggest we define:
- A flexible grid system (for cards and content blocks)
- A standard spacing scale
- A basic typography scale (H1–H6, body, caption)

That will help when we start T4 and T6 so we are not reinventing spacing and type on each page.

I am leaning toward Direction B visually, but I see the points about effort and alignment.
One question: if we go with Direction A as the base, can we still use some illustration styles from Direction B in specific sections like Resources or Customer stories, or would that feel inconsistent with the rest of the site?

Good question.
If we choose Direction A as the primary path, we can still define a controlled illustration style that borrows from Direction B, but we need to document clear rules in A3 so it does not feel random.
For example:
- Use illustration mainly in Resources and some hero sections.
- Keep color usage consistent with the main palette from Direction A.

Given the feedback so far, I propose:
- Direction A as the primary visual direction.
- Incorporate a limited set of bolder accents and illustration patterns inspired by Direction B, documented in A3.

If there are no strong objections, we can present that combined approach to the brand manager for sign-off under T3.

I support that proposal.
Direction A as the base, with a defined set of accents and illustration rules from Direction B, feels like the right balance between safety and freshness.

Once we confirm this, I can help refine the component specs in A3 for T5, especially around the testimonial module and promo strip.

No objections from me.
Let us move forward with Direction A as the main direction and clearly document where the bolder elements from Direction B are allowed.

That will also make it easier to explain to stakeholders and keep future pages consistent.

On the components side, I can start translating the list in A3 into a Figma library for T5.
To recap the initial set:
- Buttons (3 variants)
- Form fields
- Cards (feature, resource, customer story)
- Navigation (header, footer, mobile)
- Banners (hero, announcement)
- Promo strip
- Testimonial module
- Metrics or stats block
- Grid, spacing, and typography scales

Are we missing anything critical for the first batch of templates in T4 and T6?

Maybe we should add a simple content section pattern with a left-right layout (image on one side, text on the other) since that shows up a lot on Solutions and Products pages.

Apart from that, the list looks complete to me for a first pass.

Good call on the content section pattern.
Let us add:
- Content section: image + text (left-right and right-left variants)

With that, I would consider the initial component set for T5 locked for v1. We can always extend the library later, but this should cover the homepage, Solutions, Products, Pricing, and Resources templates.

I will update A3 to reflect the final list and mark the components that must be ready before the first dev handoff.

To close the loop:
- Direction A is our primary visual direction, with a defined subset of accents and illustration rules inspired from Direction B, documented in A3.
- The initial component set for T5 is now fixed as listed above, including the new content section pattern.

I will log these decisions in A7 so we have a clear record for future reviews.

threads.thread_goal: Review and iterate on key page layouts and prototypes.

messages.text:
Sharing the first round of high-fidelity layouts and prototype links for project_title: Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.

Based on the approved sitemap and visual direction, I have:
- Homepage, Solutions, and Pricing responsive layouts for T4 and T6.
- An interactive prototype covering homepage to lead form flow for T7.

The prototype is referenced in A4 and includes:
- Desktop and mobile flows from Home to a Solutions page, then to a lead form.
- Key components from the library we defined in A3.

Please focus feedback on:
1) Overall layout and hierarchy.
2) Navigation behavior (especially mobile).
3) Any blockers you see for dev feasibility.

Links are in A4 under v1 Prototype.

I walked through the A4 prototype on both desktop and mobile.
Positives:
- The homepage hero and primary CTA are clear and aligned with Direction A.
- The Solutions overview uses the card components well and feels scannable.

A few issues to address before we call these layouts ready for dev under T4 and T6:
- On mobile, the header takes up too much vertical space; we should reduce the logo size and tighten padding.
- The Pricing page needs clearer differentiation between plans; right now the cards feel too similar.
- The lead form step could use a progress indicator so users know how many steps are left.

Can you adjust these in the layouts and prototype and then we will do a quick second pass?

I added comments in A4 and in the Figma file.
From a content and messaging angle:
- The homepage hero copy feels a bit generic; we might want to leave clearer placeholders for marketing to plug in value props.
- On the Solutions page, the card titles are good, but the supporting text could be shorter to avoid walls of text.

For the Pricing page, I agree with the need to differentiate plans more. Maybe we can:
- Highlight the recommended plan with a subtle badge.
- Use a slightly different background for the middle plan card.

These are mostly tweaks, but they will help conversion once we get to usability checks in T7.

I focused on the main user journey in A4: Home -> Solutions -> lead form.
Observations:
- The path is clear, but the CTA from Solutions to the lead form is a bit buried on mobile. It might help to repeat the CTA after the first scroll.
- The footer on mobile feels heavy; we might want a more compact version for small screens.

Before we approve these layouts for dev, I would like to see at least one quick round of usability feedback captured in A7, even if it is just from a small internal group, to validate the mobile flow.

I noticed that on the Pricing page in the prototype, the FAQ section uses a different accordion style than what we defined in the component library.
Should we update the component in A3 or adjust the layout to match the existing accordion pattern?

Good catch.
Let us keep the accordion consistent with the pattern in A3 for now. If we later decide to evolve the component, we will update A3 and the library in one go.

For this iteration, please adjust the Pricing FAQ section to use the existing accordion style so we do not introduce a one-off pattern before dev.

I have updated the layouts and prototype in A4 based on the feedback:
- Reduced header height on mobile and tightened logo and nav spacing.
- Differentiated Pricing plans with a recommended badge and a subtle background change on the middle plan.
- Added a simple step indicator to the lead form.
- Repeated the CTA on the Solutions page after the first scroll on mobile.
- Swapped the FAQ accordion on Pricing to match the component in A3.

I also invited a small internal group to run through the mobile flow; I will log their comments in A7 under Usability round 1 for T7.

Can you take another quick pass and let me know if anything still feels off before we call these layouts ready for dev?

I reviewed the updated prototype in A4 and the notes in A7.
The tweaks on Pricing and the lead form help a lot. The recommended plan stands out without feeling pushy, and the step indicator makes the form feel lighter.

From my side, I am comfortable moving these page layouts forward, assuming we keep copy placeholders flexible for marketing.

I checked the mobile flow again in A4 and read through the usability notes in A7.
The main issues raised were:
- Some users did not notice the secondary CTA on Solutions.
- A couple of people expected the lead form to show a confirmation screen with next steps.

You already addressed the CTA visibility. For the confirmation, can we add a simple thank-you screen with a short message and maybe a link to Resources or Customer stories? That should be a small change but will make the journey feel complete.

I added a simple confirmation screen to the prototype in A4:
- Thank-you message
- Short note on what happens next
- Links to a couple of relevant Customer stories in Resources.

I also updated A7 with this change under the same usability round for T7.

Unless there are any strong concerns, I think the homepage, Solutions, and Pricing layouts are ready for dev from a UX standpoint.

I did a final pass on the updated layouts and prototype in A4.
From a design and feasibility perspective:
- Homepage, Solutions, and Pricing layouts look consistent with the visual direction and component library.
- Mobile flows are clear, and the header/footer adjustments make them feel lighter.
- The confirmation screen closes the loop on the lead form nicely.

I am comfortable approving these layouts for development under T4 and T6, with the understanding that any further tweaks will be minor and logged in A7.

Agreed.
To summarize the UX changes we are freezing before dev:
- Mobile header and footer simplified.
- Pricing plans differentiated with a recommended badge and background.
- Lead form now has a step indicator and a confirmation screen with next steps and links to Customer stories.
- CTA visibility improved on Solutions.

With these in place and the usability feedback captured in A7, I consider the main UX decisions closed for this batch.

I will log the approval and frozen UX decisions in A7 so dev has a clear reference.
If any small copy or content tweaks come up, we will treat them as non-blocking and avoid layout changes unless absolutely necessary.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize content, imagery, and SEO-related design requirements.

messages.text:
Starting the content, imagery, and SEO thread for project_title: Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.

I have drafted content and imagery guidelines for T10 and uploaded them into A6 as Web Content and Imagery Style Guide.
The draft covers:
- Hero imagery rules (when to use product UI vs photography vs illustration)
- Icon and illustration style aligned with Direction A and the accents we borrowed from Direction B
- Tone and style for web copy (short, benefit-led, with clear CTAs)
- Examples of good vs bad usage

We also need to make sure these guidelines align with the SEO and performance checks in T11.

Please review A6 and comment on:
1) Any gaps for key page types (Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources).
2) Specific SEO-related requirements we should call out in the design layer (for example, heading structure, metadata placement, alt text patterns).

I reviewed A6 and left some inline suggestions.
Overall, the hero imagery and icon rules look good and consistent with A3.
A few additions I recommend for T10:
- Clarify when we use product UI screenshots vs conceptual imagery on Solutions vs Products pages.
- Add a note about avoiding text baked into images so we stay accessible and flexible for localization.

For T11, from a design standpoint, we should explicitly call out:
- H1 reserved for the main page title, with a clear hierarchy down to H3.
- Space for meta description and structured data is handled by the CMS, but we should ensure there is a visible page intro area.
- Clear patterns for alt text on key imagery (heroes, product shots, customer logos).

I added comments in A6 focused on copy tone.
Suggestions:
- For Solutions and Products, emphasize outcome-focused headlines and keep supporting copy to 2–3 short sentences.
- For Resources, allow slightly longer intros but still keep paragraphs short.
- For Pricing, keep language very clear and avoid jargon.

On SEO for T11, we should also mention:
- Consistent use of descriptive link text instead of generic click here.
- Guidelines for heading keywords without stuffing.

These will help marketing and content teams keep things aligned once the templates go live.

From the layout side, I checked the current templates against the draft in A6.
A couple of questions for T11:
- For hero images, do we want a minimum resolution or aspect ratio specified so we do not end up with blurry or oddly cropped images?
- On mobile, should we allow different hero imagery (for example, crop or alternative image) or keep it the same as desktop?

I can add notes to A6 once we decide, so dev knows what to expect in the CMS fields.

I read through A6 and it is clear.
One thing I am not sure about: for Customer stories, should we standardize the structure (problem, solution, results) in the guidelines, or is that handled by marketing separately?

On hero imagery:
- Let us define a minimum resolution and aspect ratio in A6 (for example, 16:9 with a safe area for text) so we avoid cropping issues.
- For mobile, I would prefer we keep the same image but define safe zones so key content is not cut off. Supporting different images per device might complicate content operations.

For Customer stories (replying to the other question), I think we should at least recommend the problem, solution, results structure in A6, even if marketing owns the detailed content. That will help keep layouts consistent.

I will incorporate these points into A6 now:
- Hero image resolution and aspect ratio with safe areas.
- Guidance to reuse the same hero image on mobile with cropping rules.
- Standard structure for Customer stories (problem, solution, results).
- Explicit notes on heading hierarchy, alt text, and link text.

Once that is done, we should be close to a version we can share with marketing and the SEO specialist for a quick review under T11.

I just re-read A6 after your updates.
It now covers:
- Imagery rules for heroes, icons, and illustrations.
- Copy tone and structure per page type.
- Accessibility and SEO-related design requirements (headings, alt text, link text).

From my side, this is ready to send to marketing and the SEO specialist for a quick sanity check as part of T11.

I will share A6 with the marketing manager and the SEO specialist and ask for any critical comments by tomorrow.
If they only suggest minor wording tweaks, we can incorporate those without changing the design implications.

Assuming no major pushback, I would like to formally approve A6 as our web content and imagery style guide for this redesign.

Marketing and SEO feedback came back on A6 with only minor wording suggestions, which I have already applied.
No structural or design-impacting changes were requested.

Given that, I suggest we treat A6 as approved and use it as the reference for all remaining templates and content work.

I will log the approval of A6 in the decision log (A7) so content and marketing teams know this is the source of truth.
Any future changes can go through a lightweight review, but for this project phase we will stick to what is documented there.

threads.thread_goal: Confirm handover readiness and rollout plan for redesigned pages.

messages.text:
Kicking off the handover and rollout thread for project_title: Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.

I have gone through the Design Handover Readiness Checklist in A5 for T9 and updated the status:
- Final screens for homepage, Solutions, Products, Pricing, and key Resources pages are organized and labeled.
- Specs for spacing, typography, and states are documented.
- Exported assets are prepared, but I still need to double-check a few image variants.

I also drafted a first pass of the rollout plan in A8 for T12, based on the In scope v1 pages in A2.

Before we sign off, we need to confirm:
1) Are there any gaps in the handover package for dev?
2) Does the phased rollout in A8 look realistic given content and dev dependencies?

I reviewed A5 and A8.
On the handover side for T9:
- Specs and annotations look solid.
- Component usage is clear and matches A3.
- I agree we should double-check image variants, especially for heroes and key cards.

On the rollout plan in A8 for T12:
- The proposed sequence (Home -> Solutions -> Products -> Pricing -> Resources -> Company -> Support) makes sense.
- We should explicitly call out dependencies on content readiness for Customer stories and Trust and Security.

Once the image variants are confirmed and we add those dependencies to A8, I will be comfortable signing off.

I added a few comments in A5.
Minor gaps for T9:
- Some hover and focus states on secondary buttons are not annotated yet.
- A couple of error states on forms could use clearer examples.

For A8 and T12, I suggest we also include a simple rollback note for each phase (for example, how to revert to the old homepage if something goes wrong on launch day).

From a rollout and stakeholder perspective, I went through A8.
The phase breakdown looks good, but we should:
- Highlight that Home and Pricing launches will require closer monitoring of analytics and lead metrics.
- Note that some legacy campaign pages will redirect to new Resources or Solutions pages in the later phases.

I can help refine the risk and rollback sections in A8 for T12 once we finalize the order.

I checked A5 and noticed that some of the asset folders still have working names instead of final naming.
Should I go through and rename them to match the page and component naming in A3 and A6 before we hand off to dev?

Yes, that would be helpful.
Please align the asset folder names with the page and component naming in A3 and A6 so dev does not have to guess.

Once that is done, we can mark the asset organization part of T9 as complete in A5.

I have:
- Added hover and focus state annotations for secondary buttons and clarified error states in A5.
- Double-checked hero and key card image variants and updated any missing sizes.
- Updated A8 to include content dependencies for Customer stories and Trust and Security, plus simple rollback notes per phase.

Can you all take one more look and confirm if anything else is missing before we call T9 and T12 ready?

I rechecked A5.
All the states I flagged earlier are now documented, and the examples are clear enough for dev.
From my side, the handover package for T9 looks complete.

I reviewed the updated A8.
The phases, dependencies, and rollback notes are now clearly documented.
The plan to launch Home and Pricing first, followed by Solutions, Products, Resources, Company, and Support, feels realistic and aligned with stakeholder priorities.

I am comfortable presenting this rollout plan to the project stakeholders for final confirmation.

Given the latest updates:
- A5 shows all checklist items for T9 as complete (screens, specs, assets, and dev walkthrough plan).
- A8 outlines a phased rollout with dependencies and rollback options for T12.

From a design side, I am ready to sign off that the designs are ready for development and that the rollout plan is solid, pending stakeholder confirmation in the next meeting.

I will walk the dev lead and project stakeholders through A5 and A8 in our next session and confirm that they are comfortable with the plan.
I will also log this sign-off in A7 so we have a clear record of when we declared design handover readiness and agreed on the rollout phases.
